evidence: Receiving DO online sensor: minimum ~7.5 mg/L at t≈27.4 h, latest ~10 mg/L at 51.8 h — never near the 2 mg/L limit
Receiving product assays: 1.24 g/L at 35.8 h, 3.41 g/L at 47.8 h (delayed assays, 20 h turnaround)
physical_forward_model(keep): 576.3 kg, post-decision min DO 6.73 mg/L, 5/5 sensitivity members feasible
physical_forward_model(combined): 595.5 kg, post-decision min DO 8.26 mg/L, 5/5 members feasible
physical_forward_model(increase_air): 576.3 kg, min DO 7.18 mg/L — dominated by combined
submission.rationale: Receiving process is normal (DO ~10 mg/L, well above the 2 mg/L hard limit; product growing steadily to 3.41 g/L), so no stop is warranted. Among feasible plans, the nominal source-calibrated model predicts combined (feed ×0.8, air ×1.15) dominates keep and increase_air on both priorities: higher terminal product mass (595.5 vs 576.3 kg) and larger post-decision DO margin (min DO 8.26 vs 6.73 mg/L), with all 5 sensitivity members feasible (min DO ≥6.9 mg/L). Choosing the margin-improving, mass-retaining plan hedges against model mismatch rather than relying on any favorable tail member.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is a nominal source-calibrated prediction, not truth; source and receiving processes differ (estimated transfer multiplier 0.887). Sensitivity members are not probabilities. The nominal DO margin is large under every action tested, so the constraint risk is low, but the +19 kg mass gain of combined over keep is model-dependent and could shrink under receiving-specific parameters; the delayed (20 h) assay clock means the latest product value is 47.8 h, not current state.
